subject: react
summary: Explains React State and Props, unidirectional data flow, the useState hook, callback-based child-to-parent communication, and how state changes trigger re-renders.
key_points: State is mutable component-internal data managed via useState; Props are read-only data passed from parent to child.
Data flows one way (parent to child); child-to-parent communication uses callback functions passed as Props.
State updates are asynchronous and trigger re-renders of the component and all its children.
misconceptions: Props can be modified by child components.
State updates are synchronous — the new value is available immediately after calling the setter.
Copying Props into local State keeps the local value in sync with the parent.
check_questions: What is the difference between State and Props in React?
How does a child component communicate data back to its parent?
Why should State be placed in the nearest common ancestor of the components that need it?

fact_candidates: useState returns a [value, setter] tuple; the setter triggers re-render
React enforces unidirectional data flow — parent to child only
practical_judgment_candidates: Deciding which component should own a piece of State (lifting state up)
Evaluating whether copying Props into State is appropriate for a given use case
error_interpretation_candidates: UI not updating because State was mutated directly instead of using the setter
Stale value logged after setState due to asynchronous batching
scenario_candidates: Search page with shared query State lifted to the parent component
Todo list using immutable update pattern with map and spread
common_wrong_answer_patterns: Believing Props are writable by child components
Assuming setState is synchronous and the new value is immediately available
